findings[1].title.en: Nothing rebuilds the web console automatically; the numbers it shows disagree with the live ones

findings[1].evidence.en: None of the project's 13 hooks and 3 global hooks contains the string chronicler; crontab is empty; launchctl has no entries. generated_at = 2026-07-23T22:27:12Z, age 21 h. The page shows cycle 99, context 98 %, open workers 0; the live heartbeat in the same second reads cycle 107, context 22 %, workers 2.

findings[1].means.en: The defect is not that nothing rebuilds it at night, but that freshness is tied to a wave boundary rather than to the clock. The divergence is real, but the page prints, word for word, “DEAD — do not trust anything below without checking git”, and the context clock is marked DEGRADES with a note that the night continues on the other side of a roll.

findings[1].recommendation.en: Restore the DESIGNED PostToolUse debounce hook on writes to docs/lab/ (named in the original research, 05-lab-ui-mobile-autonomy.md:184; the hook is already installed in three places), plus a fallback tick.

findings[1].calibration.en: The red team never saw this file. My calibration: CRITICAL retained — the only finding that is broken and doing harm right now, and nobody chose to have the dashboard lie. Counter-argument: the page declares itself dead in a banner. DOWNGRADED BY THE WEB RED TEAM from CRITICAL to MAJOR, and the synthesiser agrees. Three corrections: (1) the median rebuild within a working shift is 45 minutes across 19 committed builds, and the 160-hour and 74-hour gaps fall BETWEEN shifts; (2) the divergence is 4.45x, not “an order of magnitude”; (3) the direction of the error — alarming — is the SAFE one by the laboratory's own standard, whose stated anti-goal is “erring towards reassurance”. The synthesiser had the sign backwards and this is now corrected.

findings[2].title.en: Spawn mechanics in the reference files describe an API that does not exist

findings[2].evidence.en: lifecycle-and-edge-cases.md:10-11 (TeamCreate, team_name + name), :13, :159; worker-cycle-template:89; SKILL.md:848 (run_in_background on the Agent tool). Confirmed by the synthesiser against the tool schema available in this session: Agent has no run_in_background parameter, team_name is marked “Deprecated; ignored”, name is unavailable to nested agents, and there is no TeamCreate tool.

findings[2].means.en: The section an agent reads first when it is about to start someone describes last-generation tooling. The instruction for spawning background verifiers — the central protection against an hour-long browser hang — is physically unexecutable.

findings[2].recommendation.en: Rewrite “Spawn mechanics” for the current harness (Agent + isolation, Bash run_in_background, TaskStop, SendMessage) and add the rule “before your first spawn, check the tool schema, not your memory”.

findings[2].calibration.en: The red team never saw this file. My calibration: CRITICAL retained — the only finding in the set that breaks literally; confirmed by me directly. DOWNGRADED from CRITICAL to MAJOR. The section opens with the caveat “Tool names depend on the harness; these are the Claude Code shapes”, which neither the auditor nor the synthesiser quoted. The failure is loud and single-step: a validation error, and the agent corrects itself immediately; the current shift spawns workers without trouble. The synthesiser additionally checked from its own session: select:TeamCreate → no matches, keyword search likewise; the caveat is that it, too, is a nested agent, so one call from the orchestrator's session would settle it definitively.

findings[3].title.en: The skills have been frozen since 10 July — the learning loop has stopped

findings[3].evidence.en: mtime of ~/.claude/skills/orchestrating-delivery-agents/SKILL.md = 2026-07-10 21:06; 37 commits in skill/ between 11 June and 10 July, and after that only remote-control; 9 of the 17 lessons in memory/ are absent from the skills.

findings[3].means.en: The core of the product stopped updating at exactly the moment the system started working in earnest. Fourteen days of experience settled into a state file and into this machine's memory — places the next orchestrator on another machine will not read.

findings[3].recommendation.en: Restore the procedure “lesson → GSL task → edit the authoritative global copy → targeted rsync global→local → commit”. Make editing the skill a mandatory item when closing a shift, exactly like the handoff.

findings[3].calibration.en: Downgraded by the synthesiser from CRITICAL to MAJOR: this is a root cause, not an acute breakage. Calibration: the “9 of 17 lessons missing” count was built on a broken baseline. The honest count is seven lessons in the skills themselves, four or five fixed outside them DELIBERATELY and in the right place (repository policy in CLAUDE.md, a machine fact in STATE, design in the spec, report format in a dedicated skill), two of those backed by a MECHANISM. Three or four of sixteen are left homeless. The procedural conclusion survived completely and was called the most valuable in the file.

findings[4].title.en: The watchdog is built, tested, and has never run in anger

findings[4].evidence.en: launchctl list has no gosleep entries; ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ has no plist; crontab is empty; docs/handoff/.watchdog-ledger.jsonl does not exist; the .artifacts/watchdog directory does not exist at all; ps shows no process; git log -- tools/watchdog/ returns 8 commits, all on 2026-07-10. Five independent confirmations.

findings[4].means.en: The second layer of supervision — the one the mandate was written for — has not been switched on for a single night. If the orchestrator stalls at night, intervention will still have to be manual.

findings[4].recommendation.en: This is a fork for you, not a task for engineers: five consecutive handoffs carried it openly as “with the owner”, and the agents' briefs explicitly forbid them to install the watchdog. The recommendation is an observation-only run with kill and re-wake disabled.

findings[4].calibration.en: The red team lowered this from CRITICAL to MAJOR and folded three labels into one finding. Accepted. A calibration on attribution: installing the watchdog is THE OWNER'S ACTION BY DESIGN. Runbook GSL-57 is written with launchctl commands marked “performed by the OWNER”; the code passed smoke 65/65; epic GSL-49 closed end to end. This is not “the skill describes a fiction” but an installation step nobody took. The conclusion for the plan is unchanged (pillar 2 is not closed by a mechanism), but the task is addressed to you, not to engineers.

findings[5].title.en: “Alive but useless” — 60.8 hours of a motionless cycle with a healthy pulse

findings[5].evidence.en: The watchdog judges liveness solely from a file's mtime and the fields of the last line. Breaking 200 heartbeat lines down by cycle value: cycle 103 — 26 lines over 11.5 hours; cycle 81 — 71 lines over 60.8 hours (2026-07-20T23:51 → 2026-07-23T12:39) with status “ok”. The cycle counter is compared with nothing: the code contains not a single read of HB_CYCLE other than writing it into the ledger.

findings[5].means.en: This is exactly the failure you described in the mandate as “it went on pause”. Any watchdog judging by file freshness would call sixty hours of standstill perfect health.

findings[5].recommendation.en: Treat as a sign of life not only a fresh mtime but also movement of the cycle counter (and any freeze of context_pct) for longer than N ticks. This costs zero tokens.

findings[5].calibration.en: The red team raised the significance: the auditor's example spanned 4.5 hours; reality is 13 times worse. Re-confirmed as the number-one finding of the whole audit. Additional empirical data from the second calibration: context_pct >= 70 in 171 pulses out of 200 with only one rolling event — that is, frozen values are observed on a mass scale.

findings[5].rank_note.en: the number-one finding of the whole audit

findings[6].title.en: The watchdog's default configuration would have started a second orchestrator beside the live one

findings[6].evidence.en: watchdog.conf is absent (only .example exists) → the defaults apply. watchdog.sh:118 — WD_TMUX_SESSION defaults to “gosleep”; tmux has-session -t gosleep → not found; the orchestrator lives in session 11, pane %193. validate_config() checks that the name is non-empty, but not that the session exists.

findings[6].means.en: A mechanism meant as a safety net would, if switched on as-is, have split the fleet in two: two orchestrators on one repository and one branch.

findings[6].recommendation.en: Have the orchestrator write a session field into the heartbeat alongside pane, and have the watchdog take the name from there — then the mismatch becomes impossible by construction. Plus a reality gate.

findings[6].calibration.en: The red team made three corrections. It only fires when open_workers ≤ 1 (92 % of lines). “The budget burns out in three ticks” is wrong — it is exactly ONE extra orchestrator, after which the identity gate returns kill_refused and escalates. The runbook makes setting the session name step 1 of installation. Lowered to MAJOR.

findings[7].title.en: Nobody applies the default when a deadline passes — the mechanism does not exist

findings[7].evidence.en: grep for “lab-emit.sh resolve” across tools/ and .claude/ → 0 matches; list --due is a pure print filter; 16 hooks lead to lab-log-hook.sh and none of them touches the queue. Empirically: q-2026-07-13-001 was applied 148.4 h after its deadline, -004 160.1 h, -005 159.8 h, all three closed in a single batch on 20 July.

findings[7].means.en: The mandate's promise — “questions pile up while the system settles the small stuff itself” — holds exactly as long as the orchestrator is alive. Once it dies the queue freezes, and in the morning you get not “here is what I decided” but “here is what stalled”.

findings[7].recommendation.en: Move applying defaults out of the pulse and into an independent process: an idempotent lab-emit apply-due command on the same tick.

findings[7].calibration.en: The red team lowered this from CRITICAL to MAJOR: it is a documented choice covered by a gate — countdown.ts prints “nobody applied the default” in so many words, and smoke.sh:1362 checks for that text. The practical harm is narrow: a dead orchestrator has no use for a default.

findings[8].title.en: The circuit breaker exists only as text inside a skill

findings[8].evidence.en: SKILL.md:779-825 — states CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN, four trip signals, a cooldown, a mandatory breaker= line in STATE. ORCHESTRATION-STATE.md contains no breaker= line (the two matches are quotes from someone else's audit). breaker.* events: 0 out of 1,933. The only mention in code is the event-name declaration at lab-emit.sh:88.

findings[8].means.en: “We have a protection against looping” is an instruction the LLM is expected to remember and execute by hand every cycle. Across roughly 104 cycles the prescribed line never once appeared. In practice there is no loop protection.

findings[8].recommendation.en: Either make the breaker mechanical (a script counts at the cycle boundary, in the same place the heartbeat is written), or honestly withdraw its “shipped” status. The in-between state is more dangerous than either.

findings[8].calibration.en: Four independent confirmations. The red team confirmed it without corrections.

findings[9].title.en: The autonomy indicator rests on a false premise written straight into the code

findings[9].evidence.en: chronicler.py:1499-1501 — “A DECISION auto-applies at its deadline and the night keeps moving”; :2077-2079 — DECISIONs “resolve themselves”. Both statements are false (see finding 7). runway.hours = null, bound = unknown, unknown_axes = [budget, work]. The context axis refers to “the watchdog forces a handoff” — and the watchdog is not installed.

findings[9].means.en: The one indicator you asked for, so you could tell whether it was safe to go to bed, answers “I don't know” — and its only concrete claim rests on two mechanisms that do not run. It is also systematically biased towards optimism: it does not count overdue DECISIONs as a stop.

findings[9].recommendation.en: Add an axis to runway for “overdue DECISIONs with no live pulse”; any axis whose mechanism is not running must report unknown rather than degrades.

findings[9].calibration.en: The red team confirmed it word for word.

findings[10].title.en: There is no permissions block at all; the orchestrator runs with --dangerously-skip-permissions

findings[10].evidence.en: .claude/settings.json contains no allow, no deny, no ask and no defaultMode (its keys are $comment and hooks). The orchestrator was started as claude --dangerously-skip-permissions (verified in ps for pid 49389 under pane %193). There are 20 notification.raised events, among them “fix-113 needs permission for Bash” and “Claude needs your permission”.

findings[10].means.en: The problem “a permission prompt ends the night” is already solved — by there being no permissions left. At night an autonomous LLM holds an unrestricted shell on your personal machine, together with gh, the Jira MCP, subscription keys in the keychain and write access to the shared tree; meanwhile agents browse the web and start third-party MCP servers.

findings[10].recommendation.en: Inventory what agents actually call, and propose a concrete permissions.allow to you instead of removing every restriction. The decision itself is question 3.

findings[10].calibration.en: The red team: the fact is worse than described, and the original recommendation (“extend the allowlist”) is unexecutable — there is nothing to extend.

findings[11].title.en: Nothing runs the chronicler: the laboratory does not rebuild itself

findings[11].evidence.en: grep for chronicler across tools/ and .claude/ → no hook, cron entry or watchdog calls it. lab-write.sh:58 asserts “The chronicler runs on every cycle boundary” — that is an intention, not a mechanism. render_bundle.json and status.json were built at 2026-07-23T22:27:12Z.

findings[11].means.en: The raw event log really is autonomous. Everything you actually look at — seven pages, the status, the mobile projection, the digest — is rebuilt only when an agent remembers. At night, the very thing all of this was built for, that will not happen.

findings[11].recommendation.en: A debounced run on SessionEnd/Stop (the hooks are already installed) plus a fallback interval tick.

findings[12].title.en: 152 of 161 tasks have no status; the tracker went 11 days unpolled, and the standard gate switches the reconciliation off

findings[12].evidence.en: tasks.by_status = {unknown: 152, Done: 5, To Do: 3, In Progress: 1}; tracker_last_polled = 2026-07-12T21:26:24Z. poll-fill.sh:29-34 requires --jira-json, and grep for jira_json across chronicler.py → 0 matches: the chronicler never passes that file. The standard shift gate uses --no-poll, which disables the reconciliation entirely. A control dry run found 6 missed events even from git/gh alone.
